- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 5–10 day horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply mean-reversion correction to mid-horizon (days 10–20) by aligning with 10-day moving average of history.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply downward bias of 1–4% to align with true volatility decay.
- If sentiment is neutral or low (≤0.33) and history shows strong mean reversion, model often misses downward correction; apply 2–5% downward adjustment for 10–30 day horizon.
